title: Ikigai
author: Héctor García and Francesc Miralles
blurb: Why do so many people on the Japanese island of Okinawa live past 100, and stay cheerful doing it? Héctor García and Francesc Miralles set out to find out, visiting the rural village of Ogimi and talking with its oldest residents. Their answer centres on ikigai, a Japanese idea that roughly means your reason for getting up in the morning. The book blends those interviews with everyday habits and ideas from psychology. It covers eating until you are about 80 percent full, moving gently every day, and staying close to friends and community. It draws on Viktor Frankl's logotherapy and Japanese Morita therapy to explore meaning, and on the idea of flow to show how absorbing activities keep us engaged. It ends with resilience, embracing imperfection, and ten simple rules for living a long, purposeful life.

lessons.t: Find Your Reason to Get Up
lessons.b: Ikigai is the personal sense of purpose that gives each day meaning, and the authors argue it is linked to living longer and happier.
